name: Nobonob
confidence_why: The only first-hand statement on Nobonob stress is one line in Aeschliman's 1992 four-page phonology data sheet, "Stress is predictable", with no placement and no stress-marked examples, and Z'graggen's 1969 and 1971 surveys left stress unmarked because its patterning was not yet established, so the record can say only that stress is non-contrastive and its position is undocumented.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (4 pp., A4, 'OPD', SIL PNG Branch, PDFMaker 2004; extracted text has a clean text). Page 3 carries, verbatim and on consecutive lines, the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' followed by the single sentence 'Stress is predictable.' Nothing else in the section; the ~150 example words, the syllable-pattern table and the transcribed text passage carry no stress marks, and no tone remark appears despite 'tone' in the heading. So the reading 'unclear or contradictory' (a first-hand statement that stress is non-contrastive, but no placement or rule) is the right slot from the fixed list; 'none found' would be wrong because a statement exists, and no fixed-* slot is supported.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only statement is that stress is predictable (i.e. non-contrastive); the source does not say on which syllable it falls, and none of the ~150 example words or the transcribed text passage is marked for stress. Tone and length are listed in the section heading but nothing is said about tone; long vowels and long consonants are written orthographically (aa, ee, ii, oo, uu; underlined p t k).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (the OPD is a citation-form phonology data sheet); no phrase-level remarks. The document is a 4-page SIL PNG 'Organised Phonology Data' summary, not a full phonology.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is headed 'Nobonob (Garuh) Language [GAW], Madang - Madang Province; Mabuso Stock; Hanseman Family; villages Nagada, Betip, Amron, Haven, Balepa, Belan, Butelkud' = nobo1238 exactly. It notes that one consonant 'is pronounced as a voiceless dental lenis aspirated plosive in some dialects' but names no dialect. Z'graggen's Garuh (language no. 7 / C28) and Dempwolff's Nupanob/Bawaipa/Misdao are the same language under older names.
